body: Jegadeesh and Titman, 'Returns to Buying Winners and Selling Losers' (Journal of Finance 48(1), 1993; ~11,500 citations), US 1965-1989: buying the past 3-12 month winners and selling the losers earned about 1% a month over the next 3-12 months, with partial reversal after 12 months. Momentum has been replicated in nearly every market and asset class (Asness-Moskowitz-Pedersen 2013), India included: IIMA WML about 10.6% CAGR 1994-2025. Daniel and Moskowitz, 'Momentum Crashes' (Journal of Financial Economics 122(2), 2016; ~960 Crossref citations): the losses are concentrated in 'panic states', after a market decline and when volatility is high, at the moment the market rebounds. The past losers (beaten-down, high-beta stocks) then rally violently. The US winner-minus-loser portfolio lost about 91% in July-August 1932 and about 73% in March-May 2009. Momentum returns are negatively skewed. A dynamic strategy that scales exposure by forecast mean and variance roughly doubles the Sharpe ratio. Replicated: yes; IIMA India crashes in 2000, 1998 and 2009 match the pattern. Use for us: (1) momentum indices (Nifty200 Momentum 30) and 'buy what is going up' are reasonable tilts but are short a crash put right after bear markets; (2) after a 30%+ market fall, the best near-term returns usually come from the junk, and momentum portfolios lag badly; (3) do not lever momentum.
title: Momentum (Jegadeesh-Titman 1993) works on average but crashes in rebounds (Daniel-Moskowitz 2016: -91% in 1932, -73% in 2009)
